title: A linear system containing ideal products is immersive
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $Y$ a $k$-scheme, $i:Z\to Y$ a closed immersion, $\mathcal I$ its ideal, and $L$ an invertible module. Schemes, closed immersions, ideals and invertible modules are as in [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], and [def-sc-invertible-module]. Let $r\le n$ be natural numbers, assume $L^{\otimes r}$ is very ample [def-sc-ample], and let $\sigma$ be global generating sections [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections] of $\mathcal I\otimes L^{\otimes(n-r)}$. Put $U=Y\setminus i(Z)$. Let $A$ be a finite index type and let $s_a\in\Gamma(Y,L^{\otimes n})$ be sections whose $k$-linear span contains every section restricting to zero on $Z$. Suppose their pullbacks $t_a$ generate $L^{\otimes n}|_U$. Then the morphism $U\to\mathbf P(A;k)$ classified by the $t_a$ [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections] is an immersion [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties].

proof.text: Choose the fixed closed immersion j:Y → P(B;k) and section-preserving isomorphism from very ampleness. Construct the ideal-coordinate products explicitly using the ideal inclusion and tensor-power isomorphism. Apply the product-coordinate relations lemma: these products vanish on Z, their restrictions cover U by generating loci, and their ratios agree with the ratios of j.

The span assumption writes every global product as a finite k-linear combination of the specified sections. Pull this identity back to U, converting k scalars through GammaSpecIso and the structure map. The generatingSections_pair theorem supplies the section-preserving universal pair for the specified morphism f. The projective pair chart frame and ratio formulas then show that on f^(-1)D_+(T_q) each product is f^*A_aqb times the q-th section, where A_aqb is the corresponding linearRatio.

At any x in U choose a product generating at x and a standard chart q containing f(x). On W=D(A_aqb) the denominator is a unit. Normalize all the linear forms by it and use homOfSections to construct h:W → P(B;k), with b-th coordinate 1. On V=f^(-1)W the q-th section is a free generator, so cancellation in the product ratio identities yields j^*(T_c/T_b) f^*A_aqb=f^*A_aqc. The normalized h and j|_V have equal base maps and coordinate ratios, hence are equal by projective-chart ratio extensionality.

The restriction V → Y → P(B;k) is an immersion, so f|_V followed by h is an immersion. Cancel h to conclude f|_V is an immersion, and compose with W → P(I;k). The chosen W contains f(x), by the free-generator criterion for the nonzero linear form. Apply target locality near the image for every x. The empty-source case is covered without a separate nonemptiness assumption.
